items.a: Yes. A person answers 24/7 at {phone}. Talk, photo and text are here for when calling isn’t convenient.

items.q: Do you work with my insurance?
items.a: We document everything — photos, moisture readings, scope — and share it with you and your adjuster. Your carrier decides coverage. You pay your deductible, nothing more.

items.q: Someone else did the drying. Can you do the rebuild?
items.a: Yes. Tell us what you have — the estimate, letters, photos — and we’ll walk the job with you.

items.q: Do you do remodels when nothing is damaged?
items.a: Yes — kitchens, bathrooms and interiors, with the same crew and the same project page.

ask.leak: Do you know of a leak in this area?

alerts.shutoff: First: shut off the water if you can do so safely.
alerts.shutoffText: If water is near outlets, cords or the electrical panel, stay out of that room.
alerts.sewage: Keep people and pets out of the water.
alerts.sewageText: Sewage can carry bacteria. Don’t try to clean it up yourself.
alerts.fire: Don’t go back inside until the fire department says it’s safe.
alerts.mold: Try not to scrub or disturb it before we look at it.

shutoff.title: Let’s find it.
shutoff.text: Only if you can reach it safely.
steps: For one fixture — toilet, sink, washer — look for the small valve on the wall behind it and turn it clockwise.
For the whole house, the main valve is usually where the water line comes in: garage, basement, crawlspace or near the water heater.
Turn it clockwise until it stops. If it won’t move, don’t force it — call us.

safety.note: Ona starts once the area is safe. We don’t replace emergency services, an electrician or your gas utility.
